searches.note: Eighteen searches of a share of twenty eight, ten left unspent. Five were restricted to a house's own domain (Errázuriz twice, Casa Marín, Viña Leyda, Matetic, Kingston); the rest blocked the house's domain and the writers' own sites the author leant on, so each second source would be independent. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.

Writers' own sites (Wine Anorak, Vinography, Wine with Seth), a critic's own tasting site and a language model's encyclopaedia were read as leads only and never cited; a Forbes column whose address names its living writers is not cited.
Edits were made in place, keeping the author's layout, and the fragment lints sound with five records refuted.

tested: The founder Maximiano Errázuriz Valdivieso, 1832 to 1890, surveyor, politician and industrialist, land bought at Panquehue in 1870: Wikipedia and the Chilean Congress library (he died at Panquehue on 17 November 1890). Sound.

The first vintage of the Founder's Reserve: Decanter's review of the 1984 calls it the first released, The World of Fine Wine calls the 1984 the first vintage and all Cabernet Sauvignon; Wine-Searcher dates the name to 1983. Changed.

The ageing: the house's sheets for 1995, 2008, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2020 and 2021 (sixteen, twenty, then twenty two months; 60 to 72 per cent new; Stockinger 2020). Sound in substance, wording set to the sheets.

The sites: the sheets of 2018 and 2020 (Max I on weathered diorite, the hillsides north and north east facing at 5 to 25 degrees, Max V an alluvial terrace under a kilometre from the river, cooler). Changed; sixty kilometres from the sea found nowhere.
Villa Don Maximiano as the second wine: the house's 2020 sheet and three merchants. Sound. The cellars of lime and stone: the house's tour page. Changed to its words.
Rules: no living person named (the family head named in the library is not), no price, no score. Cards and questions: one right answer each; the story question's distractor 1983 now explained.

records.pass: second reader of the Alazán rewrite
tested: Alazán as the flagship: the house's 2021 sheet calls it our flagship Pinot Noir; its winemaking page calls Tobiano and Alazán the original labels and the most approachable Pinot Noirs, blended from blocks and lots selected by barrel. Sound as flagship; the tiering of lots changed.
The first choice of lots for Alazán and the next tier for Tobiano: three searches of the house's own site (its winemaking and Pinot Noir pages, its wine pages) found it nowhere. Changed, cut.

The making: the sheets of 2019 (ten months, French oak, concrete egg, Austrian foudres), 2021 (eleven months) and 2022 (ten months, half foudre, two fifths barrel, a tenth egg; released September 2023), Skurnik's eight months for 2017, about 30 per cent new on the house's site. Changed to eight to eleven months.

The history: Wikipedia, the Almanac and the house's history page (the patriarch from Michigan in about 1906, no gold found, a dairy and cattle ranch, planting 1998, the first harvest of 2001 sold to other winemakers, 400 cases of Pinot Noir and Syrah under the family label in 2003). Sound, save copper, which no source names as his quarry.
Casablanca planted from 1982: several accounts credit the first vines of 1982 to the valley's pioneer winemaker. Sound.

The label word: alazán a horse of reddish coat; the house's winemaking page says the founders chose it for the flagship to match its deep red colour; a critic's note dates the family horse to the 1950s. Sound.
Serving: no sheet gives a serving temperature. Left as general service, open.

Rules: no living person named, no price, no score, nothing volatile; no judging superlative; British; no dash. Cards and questions: one right answer each, distractors plausible (1906 the patriarch's arrival, 1982 the valley's first vines, 2003 the first own label); the first question's explanation set to eight to eleven months.

swaps.proposed: Keep the house and the key; rename the wine from Tobiano Pinot Noir to Alazán Pinot Noir.
swaps.why: The house's own pages call Alazán its flagship Pinot Noir, made from the lots chosen first, and Tobiano the next tier; the owner asked for the flagship. For the read together agent, who changes plan.json and the fragment together: Alazán is Pinot Noir alone from the same western hillsides, aged about eight to eleven months in French oak barrels and concrete eggs, with Austrian oak foudres in recent vintages (the house's sheets of 2013, 2019, 2021 and 2022); the house says it chose the name for the deep red colour of a chestnut horse. The Tobiano text moves to others.
